headlines: GROUNDUP MUSIC FESTIVAL RETURNS TO MIAMI BEACH IN MARCH
SNARKY PUPPY BRINGS GROUNDUP FESTIVAL BACK TO NORTH BEACH
MIAMI BEACH BANDSHELL HOSTS STAR-STUDDED GROUNDUP MUSIC FESTIVAL
draft.article: The GroundUp Music Festival is heading back to the Miami Beach Bandshell at 7275 Collins Avenue from Friday, March 12 through Sunday, March 14. An annual South Florida staple since 2017, the festival features jazz fusion collective Snarky Puppy headlining each night. This year lineup showcases Domi and JD Beck, Lionel Loueke, Gretchen Parlato, Charlie Hunter, Ella Feingold, Victoria Canal, Lau Noah, and New Orleans funk band The Rumble. Beyond concerts and nightly Family Dinner sets, attendees can participate in daily masterclasses and panels with musicians. Following the 11 p.m. North Beach curfew, festival jams move to an unannounced venue. Single-day admission starts at $118, with weekend passes starting at $211.

headlines: MIAMI BEACH LAUNCHES 120-DAY FOOD WASTE PILOT PROGRAM
STOPPING RESTAURANT FOOD WASTE IN MIAMI BEACH
HOW MIAMI BEACH RESTAURANTS ARE TACKLING LOCAL HUNGER
draft.article: Miami Beach is rolling out a new 120-day voluntary pilot program designed to help local restaurants and food retailers redirect surplus food to community members in need. Sponsored by Commissioner Laura Dominguez and supported by Mayor Steven Meiner, the educational initiative links city kitchens with food recovery groups at no cost or liability to donors. Participating spots receive contact details for four partner organizations: Food Rescue US, Farm Share, Nourish Miami, and Feeding South Florida. Along with feeding local families facing food insecurity, the program aims to lower landfill methane emissions and cut pollution across the city. Businesses will also complete a brief survey detailing their experiences to shape future city food waste policies.

items.desc: More than half of Miami-Dade voters have cast ballots, and Democrats are out in front.

headlines: MIAMI-DADE DEMOCRATS LEAD EARLY VOTES DESPITE REPUBLICAN REGISTRATION EDGE
BLUE SURGE IN MIAMI-DADE TURNOUT
CAN MIAMI-DADE SHIFT BLUE AGAIN THIS ELECTION?
draft.article:
Miami-Dade County voters are turning out in force, with Democrats taking an early midday lead in ballots cast.

According to Supervisor of Elections Alina Garcia’s Office, over half of registered voters had participated by early Tuesday afternoon. By 1:20 p.m., 50.8% of the electorate had cast ballots. Democrats held 36.4% of those votes, followed by Republicans at 35.2% and third- or no-party voters at 28.4%.

The numbers show Democrats out front despite Republicans holding a 45,556-voter registration advantage as of October 1. County polling sites stay open until 7 p.m., and anyone waiting in line at closing time can still vote.

items.title: Guards accused of beating inmate at a state prison in Miami-Dade are sentenced
items.desc: The case involved a lieutenant and six officers.

headlines: SEVEN GUARDS SENTENCED IN SOUTH MIAMI-DADE PRISON BEATING CASE
MIAMI PRISON GUARDS AVOID JAIL TIME AFTER INMATE ATTACK
SEE HOW A SOUTH MIAMI-DADE PRISON BEATING CASE ENDED
draft.article:
Seven corrections staffers from Dade Correctional Institution, located south of Florida City in South Miami-Dade, have resolved criminal cases tied to the April 5, 2025 beating of an inmate.

Around 9:30 p.m., 31-year-old inmate Christopher Castro was escorted to an area away from security cameras and placed in a holding cell. While handcuffed, Castro was kicked and punched in the face, head, and back by officers, leaving blood on the cell surfaces.

Lieutenant Shentrica Jones Clark, 41, received six months of house arrest and six months of probation for evidence tampering. Six other officers, ages 25 to 36, must surrender their certifications and complete 50 hours of community service under plea deals with prosecutors.

headlines: LAKERS TOP MIAMI HEAT 138-117 ON MONDAY NIGHT
HEAT FALL AS LAKERS WALL OFF GIANNIS
HOW LOS ANGELES SLOWED DOWN MIAMI'S NEW SUPERSTAR TANDEM
draft.article:
The Miami Heat dropped to a 2-5 record on Monday after suffering a 138-117 defeat against the Los Angeles Lakers, ending Miami's two-game winning streak.

Los Angeles used a focused defensive scheme to slow down Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. Lakers guard Austin Reaves explained that their plan was to form a physical wall with multiple defenders, pack the paint, and push Miami's frontcourt into taking jump shots.

Antetokounmpo scored 20 first-half points on the way to 30 points, 12 rebounds, and seven assists, but the extra defensive pressure caused seven turnovers. Luka Doncic led Los Angeles with 42 points and 13 assists, while Reaves added 27 points.

headlines: DADE COUNTY WAS OFFICIALLY CREATED ON FEBRUARY 4, 1836
THE HISTORIC 1836 CREATION OF DADE COUNTY
HOW THE MIAMI RIVER HELPED NAME DADE COUNTY IN 1836
draft.article:
Dade County officially began on February 4, 1836. The county was named after Major Francis L. Dade and the Miami River, marking the formal start of our local geographic history.

During that same year of 1836, Fort Dallas was built in the area. The newly constructed outpost served as a military base during the Second Seminole War.

The year 1836 defined early regional history through the creation of Dade County, its naming after Major Francis L. Dade and the Miami River, and the strategic presence of the Fort Dallas military installation.
